deviations_from_adr: register.ts 3f-bis INSERT omits llm_endpoint/llm_model/llm_secret_handle/llm_connection_id/autonomy_threshold from the column list entirely (relying on their NULL default) instead of writing literal NULLs as the ADR §2.1 sample SQL shows — because naming llm_secret_handle anywhere in register.ts (even as a literal NULL) trips ci/checks/secret-handle-isolation.sh FF-25-3 (register.ts is not, and must not become, a T-0025 custody-allow-listed file). register.ts 3f-bis binds kc_client_id as its own parameterized value (computed in JS: `assistant-agent-${tenantId}`) rather than the ADR's inline `'assistant-agent-' || $1::text` SQL expression — Postgres raised 'inconsistent types deduced for parameter $1' when the same placeholder was bound both bare (uuid column) and ::text-cast in one statement. Caught by ci/checks/db/assistant-llm-binding.test.ts on a real Postgres run; same final kc_client_id value.

friction_events: FE-1: register.ts's original 3f-bis INSERT (per ADR §2.1's literal sample SQL) bound the SAME query parameter both as a bare uuid value and ::text-cast in one statement — Postgres rejected it with 'inconsistent types deduced for parameter $1'. Fixed by computing kc_client_id in JS as its own parameter.

FE-2: naming llm_secret_handle anywhere in register.ts (even in a literal-NULL column list, or in an explanatory code comment) trips ci/checks/secret-handle-isolation.sh FF-25-3 (T-0025 custody allow-list). Fixed by omitting the LLM-config columns from the INSERT's column list entirely (NULL-by-omission) and rewording comments to describe the columns without naming the gated one.

FE-3: the kit's EmptyState component (web/src/components/components.jsx) takes a `description` prop, not `message` — the pre-existing screen-llm-connections.jsx passed `message`, which EmptyState silently drops. Discovered while making AC-9/FF-UX-4 genuinely true (a real, hidden, pre-existing bug); fixed and regression-locked.

FE-4: this repo's `web/` test tier runs in vitest 'node' environment with no jsdom and no react-dom/react-test-renderer available — components using hooks (useState/useId/etc.) cannot be called directly as plain functions outside a React render (confirmed empirically: 'Cannot read properties of null (reading useId)'). Followed the repo's own established convention (see web/src/screens/screen-llm-connections.test.jsx's pre-existing mapTestResponse tests and web/src/forms/field-renderer.test.jsx's tree-walk pattern): pure/hook-free logic and presentational components are unit-tested directly (tree-walk, no mount); hook-bearing components/screens are covered by source-text presence assertions instead.

FE-5: production wiring (src/server.ts) runs GET /api/agents, PUT /api/agents/:id/llm-connection, and resolveActorTenant all against the SAME BYPASSRLS pool (DATABASE_URL/choros_migrator via getOrgPool()), not the NOBYPASSRLS choros_app pool — resolveActorTenant is a documented cross-tenant lookup that must run before any tenant GUC exists, so it cannot work under FORCE RLS with no GUC set. Confirmed empirically while wiring ci/checks/db/assistant-llm-binding.test.ts (pointing it at choros_app 403'd ACTOR_TENANT_UNRESOLVED); the DB test now mirrors production wiring exactly.

FE-6: this worktree was shared, without an isolated cwd, by several other spawned follow-up sessions running concurrently while this task's own fitness verification was in progress — their commits/file edits appeared and disappeared in `git status` mid-run. Handled by repeatedly reverting non-T-0574 ci/checks/*.sh and package.json edits out of the working tree before each verification pass, and by re-running the affected suites (fitness:db, unit tests) after the branch's HEAD advanced (migration 116 landing) to confirm no interaction effects.

FE-7: one ci/checks/db/doc-regen.db.test.ts test run hit a 5000ms vitest timeout during a full fitness:db pass while multiple concurrent sessions were competing for CPU/DB in the same environment; re-run in isolation (no contention) passed cleanly in 11.3s across all 17 of its tests — confirmed as environmental flakiness, not a regression (the file has zero diff in this task).
